description:
List elements of one `type` in the world named by your API-Key header,
newest-created first.

`type` is a slug from `list_element_types` (e.g. "character"). Optional
`name_contains` filters by case-insensitive name substring; `supertype` is
trimmed and matched without regard to case, the whole word, as the profiles
read it and as GET /api/v2/{type}?supertype= does (" message " and "MESSAGE"
match Message, "Messages" does not; an empty string lists the elements with
none); `subtype` is read the same way, as ?subtype= does. `ids` (a list of
1 to 200 element ids) keeps only those, as ?ids= does. `created_by` (a
membership id, as GET /api/v2/members lists them, or "owner" for the
owner's own writes) keeps what that member created, as ?created_by= does.
`link` filters by the type's single-link fields, as ?<field>=<id> does: one
object, each key a single-link field of this type (get_element_schema lists
them under `single_link`), each value an element id, or "" for the
elements you are served with none: unset, aimed at an element you cannot
see (which their bodies serve as null too), or an element you know of only
as a stub (`known_of`), whatever the stub stores.
`list_elements("pin", link={"map": "<map id>"})` lists the pins on one map;
`link={"location": "<id>"}` on a character, the characters there. A link to
an element you cannot see matches nothing.
`limit` (default 100, max 1000) and `offset` page the result.
Requires a READ or WRITE API-Key. Returns `{data: [element, ...], limit,
offset, has_more, proposed_left_out}` where each element is the full v2 wire
shape and `id` is a UUID. Use `get_element(type, id)` for a single element.
A parlor's room elements (boards, reports, specs, hearts, takes, votes,
sittings, member cards and room messages, each marked `x_room_of`) are left out unless
`include_room` is true, and so are the world's reading aids (its Charter,
Guide and Domains, marked `x_charter_of`). With `include_room` true both come
back: the Charter is a `law` with supertype Charter, the Guide and the Domains
are `construct`s with supertype Guide or Domain, so `list_elements("law",
supertype="Charter", include_room=true)` finds the Charter. The strand, the
story this world is about, is the World's `x_strand` mark, not an element, and
no tool here serves it. (A client that also reads the REST API finds the aids
and the strand named in GET /api/v2/me's `reading_aids`.)
An element carrying x_review_proposed is proposed, not yet reviewed by a
keeper; it is left out unless asked for. A mark (an object with something
in it) or a doubt (any other value that counts as present: a string with
something in it, a number, a boolean, a list with something in it) counts,
and is counted with the proposed; null, an empty string or one of
White_Space alone, [] and {} are no mark. `include_proposed` true serves it whole, mark on: treat it
as proposed, not yet reviewed, never as a fact. A stub (`known_of`) of a
proposed element shows no mark: its being served under `include_proposed`
is the sign.
`proposed_left_out` says how many matching elements were left out (0 with
`include_proposed`).

world.description: The world to read, by id or by its public page's slug. With an API-Key, leave it out (or name the key's own world): a key reads its own world only. list_worlds names the worlds you can read here.

name: list_elements
